reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $62,964.3 - this window's low, made at 09:45Z. The line moves DOWN 79.1 points from endday's 63,043.4 because that level has already done its job: it fired, price settled under it four times, and a level price is trading through is no longer an exit, it is a range boundary. Placing the new exit at the low that was MADE and then held is the one habit in this file that demonstrably works - it has now survived on three of the last four sessions where it was applied - and it keeps the exit 118.3 points ABOVE the 62,846.3 invalidation, which leaves room for the invalidation to mean something separate. A break here would confirm the lower-low sequence that started this window rather than merely opening it.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $63,309.4 - the three-day floor that broke on 13 August and has capped every attempt since - with aggregate BTC open interest NOT falling across the same bar. The gate is held UNCHANGED for a SEVENTH consecutive session and is now untested seven times running. The open-interest half of the condition finally moved in its favour this window: OI rose 0.62% to $2,134,314,696 after five consecutive declines, the first increase in the series. The price half moved AGAINST it: the window high of 63,155.8 fell 153.6 points short and was lower than endday's high. The morning session twice proposed moving this gate down to the 63,150 band on the grounds that a gate price never reaches is decoration rather than a gate. That argument is now stronger, not weaker - seven untested sessions is not a sample of bad luck - but moving a structural gate mid-week destroys the calibration series it exists to produce, so it stands one more session and the midday session should decide it.

decisionBox.changed: Position steps UP from HOLD to ADD, and it is a deliberately SMALLER step than the ones that came before it. The wallet buys a 12 USDT spot tranche at 63,063.4 against 20, 15 and 10 USDT on the three 15 August tranches - the ladder keeps shrinking as location degrades, which is the discipline that has kept every wrong call this week under three cents. Three things justify buying at all. Price at 63,063.4 sits 217.1 points above the 62,846.3 invalidation and 99.1 points above the window low, so the entry is nowhere near the forced selling. Settled funding fell for a SIXTH consecutive period to +0.004589%, the cheapest carry of the week and 54% below the 14 August 16:00Z period, so the cost of being long is at a series low. And the spot book's average entry is 63,560.0, well above market, so any tranche here improves the long-term core's basis rather than chasing it. Three things justify keeping it small and moving the tilt to BEARISH. The window made a lower low AND a lower high, which breaks the sequence endday built its bullish tilt on. The 1H MACD line crossed back BELOW zero to -15.63 from +9.31 and the histogram flipped to -10.39 from +5.46, so endday's single most constructive print reversed inside thirteen hours - the third time in four sessions this desk has had to void a constructive positioning call. And price still trades below every EMA on the 1H, 4H and daily - 1H 63,053.9/63,106.8/63,306.0/63,683.8, 4H 63,222.4/63,618.7/63,851.5/63,681.2, daily 63,887.9/64,414.0/66,508.1/72,148.8, the last of which puts spot 12.59% under its 200-day. The one genuinely new thing is that leverage started coming back: open interest rose 0.62% after five straight declines, and the long/short account ratio ticked to 2.22-2.23 and HELD there across six consecutive hourly buckets against 2.20 at endday. Yesterday's recorded lesson was that a single-reading reversal in a positioning series is noise, so the bar is six readings plus a corroborating OI print, and this clears it. That cuts both ways: returning leverage gives an advance sponsorship it did not have, and it also rebuilds the fuel that gets flushed. No resting stop is recommended because the wallet carries no leveraged position, the spot book is a long-term core with no stop by design, and the next scheduled report is midday at 12:40 COT, roughly four hours away - a watched window, not an overnight gap.

calibration.note: Endday's reduce line at 63,043.4 DID fire, and it fired harder than any level this week: the 09:00Z 1H bar settled at 62,986.1, and the 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z bars settled at 63,009.1, 63,012.4 and 63,010.6 - four consecutive settles below a published exit with no reclaim on any settled bar. Every prior break this week was reclaimed within one or two hours. Its add gate at 63,309.4 was not approached, the window high of 63,155.8 falling 153.6 points short, so the open-interest condition went untested for a SEVENTH consecutive session. Despite the reduce line firing, the session is marked YES and the reasoning is specific rather than generous. Endday's actual decision was to HOLD three existing tranches behind a resting stop at 62,830.0 and to decline a fourth. The stop was never threatened - the window low of 62,964.3 stopped 134.3 points above it, so the level did exactly what it was placed to do, which is survive a wick into the fuel and only trigger on a structural break. Acting on the reduce trigger instead would have sold spot near 62,986.1 and spot now marks 63,063.4, so obeying the exit would have cost 77.3 points; NOT obeying it was correct. The declined fourth tranche would have gone on at 63,060.2 and marks +3.2 points, +0.005%, so declining it cost essentially nothing either. The mark on the held book is +3.2 points on 0.0020118 BTC, roughly +0.0064 USDT - the first positive mark in three sessions, and the smallest number in this file, which is the point. Two endday claims must be recorded as WRONG on data within thirteen hours. Endday called the 1H MACD line crossing above zero to +9.31 the single most constructive individual print in the report; it crossed back below to -15.63 and the histogram flipped to -10.39. Endday built its bullish tilt on a higher low and a higher high; this window made a lower low at 62,964.3 and a lower high at 63,155.8 and broke the sequence. In fairness to that report, it flagged the exact mechanism of its own failure - it wrote that a zero-cross arriving as the impulse dies usually marks the end of a bounce - so the error is one of weighting rather than of observation. The recorded lesson is that when a report names the reason its own headline signal might be false, that reason should reduce the confidence attached to the signal, not sit beside it as a caveat.
